historyReviewBoundary: All 115 histories have author source checks. Final independent review covered metadata and numerical checks for all 115 classes, 12 deeper class targets and source-gap samples in seven classes. It did not independently verify every passage of every cited source.

history.name: Nitroimidazole antibacterials

starting.description: A naturally produced antibiotic, azomycin, was observed to have antimicrobial and later antitrichomonal activity. According to the 1978 history, this observed lead stimulated the preparation and testing of accessible 5-nitroimidazole isomers. A separate 1956 laboratory experiment directly reported azomycin's antitrichomonal effect, without establishing which experiment motivated the French program.

inspiration.description: The first lead was natural azomycin and its observed activity against microorganisms, including Trichomonas. A separate later observation of clinical benefit in gingivitis motivated antibacterial follow-up of the synthetic medicine.

steps.description: Azomycin was obtained from microbial culture and identified as 2-nitroimidazole; its bacteriostatic activity was experimentally examined.

Recognizing antitrichomonal activity in azomycin supplied a lead for the preparation and testing of accessible 5-nitroimidazoles; metronidazole was selected from a series for its activity-to-toxicity balance and introduced for trichomoniasis. Horie's separate 1956 experiment directly documented the natural lead's antitrichomonal activity.
A clinical gingivitis observation attributed to Shinn in 1962 motivated a 1964 study of 15 patients; the investigators also examined the compound against oral spirochetes and a Bacteroides strain.

By 1972 investigators had tested metronidazole against anaerobic and microaerophilic isolates and reported initial treatment of anaerobic infections, while emphasizing that this use remained experimental. A later editorial describes its establishment for anaerobic infections.

design.description: Researchers prepared and tested more accessible 5-nitroimidazoles related to the natural 2-nitroimidazole lead and selected the hydroxyethyl-substituted metronidazole for its balance of activity and toxicity; this was a positional and substituent change, not merely a delivery modification.

circumstances.description: Preparation and testing of the synthetic 5-nitroimidazole series was planned; the distinct clinical observation that directed attention to gingivitis was described as incidental and prompted a deliberate follow-up study.

limits: The founding chemical lead was the natural 2-nitroimidazole azomycin; metronidazole is a substituted synthetic 5-nitroimidazole. The antitrichomonal lead and the later antibacterial clinical finding are distinct observation-led stages, not separate design-from-scratch branches.

Horie's 1956 study separately documented azomycin's antitrichomonal activity; no evidence in that paper links his experiment to Rhône-Poulenc's program. The source for that causal link remains the 1978 editorial.

The assigned frozen cohort contains metronidazole only. This account does not reconstruct the individual histories of later analogues or establish that other independently founded nitroimidazole families share every step.

The first azomycin producer is described by Nakamura as Nocardia-like, while subsequent azomycin-producing Streptomyces cultures are also reported. The organism descriptions concern distinct isolations rather than a demonstrated disagreement.
gaps: The 1978 editorial is the read source for the explicit natural-lead-to-synthetic-series causal link; contemporaneous research notes and Cosar and Julou's 1959 experimental paper were not read. The 1959 paper was located at https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/13627590/ with no abstract.

Shinn's 1962 Lancet letter was located but not read; Davies and colleagues' 1964 paper is a near-contemporaneous secondary account of his observation. The frequently repeated coincident-infection anecdote has not been established from the original.
The initial 1953 Maeda, Osato and Umezawa azomycin report was located at https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/13152032/ as metadata without an abstract and was not read.

humanContributionInterpretation.summary: Improvement of Vincent's gingivitis during metronidazole treatment helped prompt anaerobic-infection investigation.
humanContributionInterpretation.scope: This is a later clinical direction; azomycin and initial nitroimidazole discovery came from laboratory work.
